paper.central_claim: A coding-agent loop that watches a robot fail, writes skills or installs external models and tests every change in simulation, run for 123 rounds on RoboCasa household tasks, discovered real capabilities (active viewing) but its improvements did not add up: the target fridge task never succeeded. The agent was rarely the bottleneck; three surrounding factors were: chained perception modules do not represent relations (semantic displacement), skill chains lock learning onto the first step, and the harness (evaluators, gates, memory) decides what the agent learns.
paper.title: What Stops Recursive Self-Improvement in Robotics? Lessons from 123 Rounds of Agentic Skill Discovery

signatures.object: The robot's software library (task programs, skills with typed implementations and routing rules, external perception/planning model providers) improved by Codex-CLI GPT agents; before-state is the library at round t.
signatures.information: Proposer sees the failure table, the evaluator's diagnosis (derived from privileged simulator state), execution traces and diffs of earlier attempts and RGB keyframes of failed steps; the robot perceives via head and wrist RGB-D and joint readings; the harness (evaluators, tests, memory, actuator description) is editable only by humans.
signatures.operation: Collect rollouts -> evaluator judges declared steps -> group first failures into gaps -> proposer writes code or files a model request -> research agent installs/probes/registers models -> test and accept -> next round starts from the improved library; routing refit from logged calls.
signatures.output: Accepted skill changes (57), registered providers (86), refitted routing, new task programs.
signatures.conditions: RoboCasa kitchen, PandaOmron mobile manipulator; Fridge (about 15 steps), Cabinet, Sink; four scene seeds; one simulator and layout.
signatures.feedback: Evaluator diagnoses and traces; rejected attempts return execution traces after later harness repairs.
signatures.selection_rule: Replay the exact recorded failure, then paired old-vs-new trials on fresh scenes and a held-out task; later sealed transfer states and regression/invariance checks; thresholds and reproduction rules were revised by humans during the run.
signatures.persistence: Library and routing on disk, orchestrator keeps its best programs; typed memory of hypotheses added later.
signatures.later_use: Next-round rollouts of the three tasks; held-out cabinet-to-counter used only in gates.
signatures.claimed_effect: No gain at the task level: Fridge 0/486, Cabinet 0/256, Sink 14/230 (9 with failed intermediate steps) despite 57 accepted changes; retained local wins (round 118 grasp) did not move task success.
signatures.failure_boundary: Evaluator capture, noisy and under-resolved gates, evidence fixed point, lost requests, registered models never called, human repairs of 113 harness faults.

signatures.object: Diagnostic framework for self-improving loops: representability, expressibility, resolvability plus a chain model of task success (Eq. 1).
signatures.information: Round-by-round records and dissections of the single run.
signatures.operation: Place each problem front of the run on the three conditions; derive frontier lock from success = product of step probabilities.
signatures.output: Three lessons and twelve design implications D1-D12 with falsifying experiments.
signatures.conditions: One run; framework described as simple and descriptive.
signatures.feedback: n/a: analytical framework, no loop of its own
signatures.later_use: n/a: descriptive framework; its recommendations are untested
signatures.claimed_effect: Explains why accepted changes do not raise task success; recommendations untested.
signatures.failure_boundary: No controls, replicates or ablations; mechanisms from records.

gap.author_gap: Coding agents improve software in loops (Voyager, Eureka, DGM) and the idea has reached robots (RHO, ASPIRE, ENPIRE); the paper asks whether such loops compound on a household manipulation task and, if not, what stops them and whether a stronger agent would fix it.
gap.checked_gap: Specific and consequential: positive reports exist, but a long fully recorded failing run with measured mechanisms is a distinct, falsifiable contribution. The conditions are framed after the fact from one run.
lineage: RHO, ASPIRE, ENPIRE (robot self-improvement with coding agents)
gap.closest_adjacent: ASPIRE (diagnosable traces, validated skill library) and ENPIRE (reset and verification module) report large gains; the authors read these as consistent with the harness deciding what the agent can achieve.
gap.residue: Open-instruction relational perception, long skill chains, and harness-side learning in a fully recorded robot loop.
gap.stakes: Accepted-change counts measure activity, not progress; human harness repair outnumbers accepted changes about two to one.
gap.method_response: A fully instrumented 123-round run plus a three-condition analysis and falsifiable recommendations.
gap.remaining_gap: Whether the recommendations (D1-D12) work; replicates, other agents and budgets; real robots.
unresolved: Whether a different proposer or budget would have solved the task is explicitly unknown.

tactic_steps_checked: identify the implicit assumption: that the software-style conditions (failures representable, fixes expressible, tests resolvable) carry over to robot self-improvement (met, E025/E023)
violate it with a constructed run: 123 rounds with human repair of the harness only (met)
re-derive/demonstrate: three conditions, frontier-lock model and Table 2 attribution (met as framework, empirical not proven)
success_checks: Violated condition shown in the real setting by measurement: met (Table 5)
Prior methods shown to fail because of the assumption: partial (prior systems are not rerun; reported gains are cited)
Violation packaged as a systematic template rather than a one-off: met (three conditions, D1-D12 with falsifiers)
failure_checks: Violation not validated against an adaptive counterpart: met as risk (a single run, no alternative agent or budget)
Bundle of changes without isolating the load-bearing one: met as risk (harness repairs, models and providers changed together)
Differentiated from near-identical prior pivots: met (RHO/ASPIRE/ENPIRE discussed)
matches.reason: The paper audits the load-bearing assumption of agentic self-improvement (that software's representability, expressibility and resolvability hold for robots) and demonstrates the violation. No C01-C29 sub-card fits: those clusters pivot theoretical, security, identifiability or optimisation assumptions, not an assumption about the selection side of a self-improving system; sub_id is null rather than forced.

rs_pattern.reason: assumption_audit_and_pivot (violate an assumption with a constructed exploit/counterexample) chosen over controlled_diagnostic_design (no confound is isolated; the study is uncontrolled) and characterize_limit_then_surpass (no formal limit is proved and no augmented operator beats it).

executes_pattern.reason: Assumption identified and violated with measured evidence; pivot to remedies is hypothesised but untested.

resolves_problem.reason: The paper states the recommendations were not tested and that it cannot say whether another agent or budget would succeed.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Auditing the assumption that agent edits plus a test gate compound corresponds to running the K401 loop (propose edits from traces, accept by gate, persist) long enough to measure that the retained edits do not move the target task.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: K401 revises harness code around a frozen agent model; here the agent revises the robot's skills and models while humans own the harness, so the mapping holds only for the propose-gate-retain structure. No sub-card of the RS parent is claimed.

claims.text: The loop's improvements did not add up: the target task never succeeded despite 57 accepted changes.
claims.setting: RoboCasa Fridge, Cabinet and Sink tasks, four scene seeds each, 123 rounds, GPT agents via Codex CLI.
claims.selection_vs_test: Gates used fresh scenes and a held-out task; reported outcomes are native task success in later rounds.
claims.result: Fridge 0/486, Cabinet 0/256, Sink 14/230 with 9 having failed intermediate steps; 57 accepted changes (51 perception).
counterevidence: Phase 1 produced a deployed active-search skill and eight called models.
claims.allowed_conclusion: In this run, accepted changes produced no task-level gain on Fridge and Cabinet.

claims.text: Semantic displacement: a code-writing agent fills the missing relational semantics with growing geometric rules that never converge.
claims.setting: Fridge region grounding; 27 attempts on a two-state gap.
claims.baseline: A 7B VLM queried on recorded views (feasibility only).
claims.result: 33 thresholds in 3,056 lines; rescue of one seed in all trials and none of the other; VLM correct in 4/4 recorded views.
counterevidence: VLM check covers a handful of views, not a benchmark.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Consistent with displacement for this front; generality is a hypothesis.

claims.text: Frontier lock: learning concentrates on the first failing step of a chain.
claims.result: 57% of fridge rollouts fail step 1; 0.9% pass five steps; round-118 grasp win reproduced but followed by 0/60 task successes.
counterevidence: No intervention such as resetting past the frontier was run.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Evidence is concentrated at the first steps, and a retained local gain did not reach the task.

claims.text: What the agent learns is decided by the harness (evaluator capture, unresolvable gates, evidence fixed point, memory corruption, capability not use, framing).
claims.result: 276 reachable successes within 1 mm of a 0.85 m sphere; 16/36 disagreeing pairs not reproduced; identical outcomes in rounds 90-102; 11 models never called; 0/8 vs 11/12 edits after a prompt paragraph changed.
counterevidence: The framing result is confounded with the round.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Several harness-side faults demonstrably shaped what the loop optimised; the relative weight of harness versus proposer is not established.

claims.text: The agent was rarely the bottleneck.
claims.result: Raising reasoning effort 'changed nothing visible'; no alternative agent run.
counterevidence: The authors state they cannot say whether a different agent, more compute or a different library representation would have solved the task.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Not established as a causal claim.

claims.text: The agent can discover a missing capability from failures alone.
claims.setting: Phase 1 (rounds 1-36) after the evaluator reported target visibility.
claims.result: Active-viewing model requested, repaired and wrapped; out-of-view failures disappeared by round 16.
counterevidence: Required an evaluator fix by humans first.

assessment.evidence_level_note: Closed-loop simulation with per-rollout task success; the evaluator for steps uses privileged state; no real robot or transfer; the central claim is negative.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In one 123-round run on three RoboCasa tasks with GPT agents, 57 accepted library changes and 86 provider registrations did not produce task successes on Fridge (0/486) or Cabinet (0/256) and only mostly accidental successes on Sink (14/230); measured records show evaluator capture, evidence concentrated at early chain steps, under-resolved gates, lost requests and uncalled models. These mechanisms are identified from records, not tested causally.
unresolved: Whether a different agent, budget or library representation succeeds.
Relative effect sizes of the three lessons.
Generality beyond one simulator, one layout and three tasks.

status_reason: Full text including all appendices read; claim_type taken as system_method with a negative/diagnostic central claim evaluated against its own scope statement.

evidence.quote: It watches a robot fail, works out which capability is missing, writes new skills or finds and installs external models, tests every change in simulation, and repeats, with no human writing robot code.
The bad news is that its improvements did not add up.
Our rule was that humans can repair the harness but never write a skill, program or model wrapper.
evidence.support_explanation: Selection side of the loop (harness) is human-only; the agent edits skills/programs/models.

evidence.locator: Sec 2 How a change is accepted
evidence.quote: A proposed code change must pass a sequence of physical tests. First, it replays the exact recorded failure with the change swapped in; did it fix what it claims to fix? Second, it runs paired trials, old against new, on fresh scenes and on a held-out task the proposer never sees
evidence.support_explanation: Selection rule for retaining a change: exact-failure replay, then paired fresh-scene and held-out trials.

evidence.locator: Sec 2 How a change is accepted
evidence.quote: The evaluator judges each declared step with privileged simulator state and returns a short diagnosis
evidence.support_explanation: Information: the step evaluator uses privileged simulator state; the robot perceives through RGB-D only.

evidence.quote: All three agents (orchestrator, proposer and research agent) are OpenAI GPT models run through the Codex CLI, each session in its own sandboxed container (Table 1 ).
The model and its reasoning effort changed twice during the run, both times by our decision, not the agent’s
evidence.support_explanation: The agent configuration changed within the run.

evidence.quote: Target task never completed Fridge 0/486; Cabinet 0/256; Sink 14/230, of which 9 had failed intermediate steps
57 accepted library changes (51 perception); 86 provider registrations over 20 identities; 847 proposal attempts
evidence.support_explanation: Activity counts: accepted vs attempted changes.

evidence.quote: This is one long run on one simulator, one kitchen layout and three tasks, with no independent replicates, matched-budget baselines or ablations.
evidence.support_explanation: Scope and design limits stated by the authors.

evidence.quote: Harness repairs, model versions and providers changed along the same timeline, so our analysis identifies mechanisms from records and dissections, not causal effect sizes.
evidence.support_explanation: Confounded timeline; mechanisms are identified from records.

evidence.quote: Region skill: 3,056 lines, 33 thresholds; composed localizer: 5,032 lines, 48 thresholds; 27 attempts on the two-state fridge gap rescued seed 69 in every trial and seed 68 in none
Qwen2.5-VL 7B placed “the top shelf” and “the shelf below” correctly in 4/4 recorded head views, about 1 s per query
evidence.support_explanation: Feasibility check of the proposed model-class change.

evidence.quote: Fridge : 57% fail step 1; 2.7% pass four steps; 0.9% pass five.
Round-118 grasp change: reproduced wins on a fresh support state and a held-out state; next 60 rollouts: 0 task successes
evidence.support_explanation: A retained local gain with no task-level effect.

evidence.quote: 276 reachable successes at 0.849–0.850 m under a 0.85 m sphere; torso absent from the action description (34 proposer complaints); base speed advertised 0.0016 m/step, measured 0.037
119 rejected candidates had rescued at least one exact state; 22 promotions (rounds 40–65) with 0 wins and 0 losses; 16 of 36 re-run disagreeing pairs did not reproduce
Identical fridge and cabinet per-seed outcomes in rounds 90–102
88 request-bearing proposals gated as code (46 on the fridge-region front); gap declined 15 times citing the lost request
evidence.support_explanation: Memory corruption: requests recorded as failed attempts.

evidence.quote: 11 provider identities first registered in rounds 114–121 have zero later collection calls
0/8 edits in rounds 93–94 vs. 11/12 in round 96 after one paragraph of proposer text changed
113 numbered harness fixes (Fig. 5 b)
Whether an accepted change raises S depends on three conditions. None of them concerns the proposer’s coding ability.
learning concentrates on the first failing link because only there is evidence plentiful and gates resolvable, and the rest of the chain stays under-trained no matter how many rounds run.
In software self-improvement the three hold almost for free.
evidence.support_explanation: Assumption audited: software-style self-improvement properties carry over to robots.

evidence.quote: Our study complements them with a long, fully recorded run that did not reach its goal
evidence.support_explanation: Positioning against RHO, ASPIRE and ENPIRE that report gains.

evidence.quote: They come from this experiment but were not themselves tested in it, so Table 3 pairs each with an experiment that could prove it wrong.
A round took one to three hours, plus several hours when models were researched, and we ran 123 rounds.
The program’s own place steps had failed, the gripper opened elsewhere, and the object happened to fall into the sink.
evidence.support_explanation: Audit of accidental successes: native task success versus correct execution.

evidence.quote: The vision-language check in § 5 covers a handful of recorded views and shows feasibility, not benchmark performance.
evidence.support_explanation: Limit of the VLM feasibility check.

evidence.quote: By round 16 the robot searched when it could not see its target, and out-of-view failures disappeared.
evidence.support_explanation: The one front where the loop produced a retained, deployed capability.

evidence.quote: Eight agent-introduced models (grasp generation, motion and base planning, active viewing, relational localization) were used in deployment.
evidence.support_explanation: Retained model additions that were actually called.

evidence.quote: Most rejections come from replaying the exact recorded failure. Of the differences that were re-run, nearly half did not reproduce.
This is a report of one long experiment, not a controlled study (§ 10 ).
Three recent systems are closest to ours.

G.reason: A specific, consequential question (does software-style self-improvement compound for robots, and if not, what stops it) with ancestors and nearest robot systems named and the remaining gap bounded (single run; remedies untested).

M.reason: The three-condition framework and chain model give distinguishable, falsifiable predictions (Table 3) and are tied to measured fronts; they are post hoc from one run and described as non-predictive.

X.reason: Roles, information access, gates, models, round cadence and the human-repair rule are reconstructable with round-by-round records; the harness, thresholds and agent configuration changed during the run and prompts/code are not provided.

E.measurement.reason: Native simulator task success with explicit denominators, an audit of accidental sink successes, and per-measure counts in Table 5; the step evaluator uses privileged state and was itself repaired many times, so step-level diagnoses changed over time.

E.causality.reason: Several mechanisms have direct measurements (evaluator sphere, uncalled models, lost requests), but there are no controls, replicates, matched-budget baselines or ablations and the timeline is confounded, so causes are inferred from records.

E.holdout.reason: Held-out task, fresh scenes and sealed states gate changes, overfitting to replayed states is reported, and the claims are confined by the authors to one simulator, layout and three tasks; no positive held-out generalisation was obtained.

E.statistics.reason: Exact counts per round and aggregate with failure-step denominators and reproducibility checks of paired differences (16/36 not reproduced), but a single run, four seeds and no intervals or variance of the loop.

E.cost.reason: Time per round, rounds, attempts and human repairs are reported (113 fixes, about twice the accepted changes); no token or dollar totals and no budget comparison.

provenance.notes: session_id/receipt_ref null: the internal Subagent cannot read its own session id or a call receipt. Blind boundary kept: no other seat, aggregate, other batch, archive, old score/Reel or assignments.jsonl was read. Domain cards R05/R06 etc. cite some batch papers as board-induced sources; those card statements were not used as evidence, all judgements come from the pinned full text.
